summary.gist: The AI semiconductor trade broke on Friday as Broadcom's guidance miss collided with a blowout jobs report, sending the Nasdaq down 4% and the Philly Semiconductor Index into its worst session since March 2020. The dominant force is rate repricing - markets are now pricing a Fed hike rather than cuts, and the 10Y at 4.55% is punishing duration-heavy growth names. The directional bet for Monday is continued weakness in semis with rotation into defensives, energy, and short-duration value.

executive_summary: Friday's session delivered the worst tech sell-off of 2026 as a one-two punch of Broadcom's disappointing AI chip guidance and a red-hot May jobs report sent the Nasdaq down 4.18% and wiped $1.3 trillion from semiconductor stocks. The PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged 10%, its steepest single-day decline since March 2020, with Marvell (-17%), Broadcom (-14%), Micron (-13%), and AMD (-11%) leading losses. Treasury yields surged - the 10Y hit 4.55% - as 172K nonfarm payrolls (vs. 80K expected) revived rate hike expectations under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting on June 16-17. Oil pulled back to Brent $94/WTI $91 despite ongoing Iran tensions, as the risk-off rotation overwhelmed the geopolitical bid. Gold held near $4,500/oz as a safe haven. Heading into next week, May CPI on June 10 is the critical data point - a hot print could cement the rate hike narrative and extend the sell-off.

macro_events.title: May Nonfarm Payrolls Crush Expectations: 172K vs 80K
macro_events.causal_chain: 172K jobs added (vs 80K expected) with unemployment steady at 4.3% and average hourly earnings +0.3% MoM -> labor market too strong for cuts -> Fed funds futures reprice from 65% hold to rising hike probability -> 10Y Treasury yield spikes 6bps to 4.55% -> higher discount rate crushes high-multiple growth stocks -> Nasdaq -4.18%, PHLX Semi Index -10% -> risk-off rotation into defensives and value -> VIX spikes, put volume surges on QQQ/SMH
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-centric but global impact via rate differentials strengthening DXY, weakening EM currencies
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2023 hot jobs report - 10Y spiked to 4.8%, Nasdaq fell 5% over following week before stabilizing
macro_events.counterargument: May payrolls may be revised lower (common in recent cycles); one data point does not make a trend; Fed may still hold if CPI softens

macro_events.title: Broadcom AI Chip Guidance Miss Triggers Sector Rout
macro_events.causal_chain: AVGO Q2 revenue $22.19B beat estimates but Q3 AI chip guidance $16B vs $17.2B expected -> unchanged FY2026 AI semi forecast signals demand plateau -> narrative shifts from AI capex acceleration to AI capex peak -> sell-the-news reaction cascades across supply chain -> MRVL -17%, MU -13%, AMD -11%, ASML -3.8% -> $1.3T wiped from chip sector -> passive fund rebalancing amplifies selling -> sentiment contagion to broader tech
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global semiconductor supply chain - US designers, Taiwan foundries (TSM), European equipment (ASML), Korean memory (Samsung, SK Hynix -6-10%)
macro_events.historical_analog: Cisco's 2000 guidance miss marked the beginning of the end for the dot-com infrastructure trade; more recently Meta's Feb 2022 guidance miss triggered -26% overnight
macro_events.counterargument: AVGO Q2 AI revenue actually grew 143% YoY to $10.8B - the miss is relative to stretched expectations, not absolute demand destruction; hyperscaler capex budgets remain committed

macro_events.title: Fed Leadership Transition: Warsh's First FOMC June 16-17
macro_events.causal_chain: Kevin Warsh replaced Powell as Fed Chair on May 15 -> first FOMC meeting in 10 days -> deeply divided committee inherits 3.8% CPI and hot labor market -> markets pricing 65% hold but hot jobs data shifting odds toward hike -> policy uncertainty premium increases -> implied volatility in rate-sensitive assets rises -> financial conditions tighten preemptively
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US policy but global impact through dollar strength and capital flows
macro_events.historical_analog: Bernanke's first FOMC in 2006 - markets were uncertain about new chair's hawkishness, leading to elevated volatility in rate markets for 2-3 meetings
macro_events.counterargument: Warsh may signal continuity rather than surprise; the Fed typically avoids dramatic moves at a new chair's first meeting to build credibility

affected_tickers.reason: Hawkish surprise risk weighs on long bonds
Uncertainty bid supports gold as hedge

macro_events.title: Iran/Middle East Tensions Keep Oil Risk Premium Elevated
macro_events.causal_chain: US-Iran negotiations stalled + Israel-Lebanon ceasefire uncertainty -> Strait of Hormuz risk persists (20M bbl/day, 20% of global oil) -> war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs remain elevated -> Brent $94/WTI $91 with $5-8 geopolitical premium baked in -> energy sector outperforms despite broader sell-off -> tanker rates stay elevated -> Asian refiners hedge via long-dated crude contracts
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East origin, global impact through energy prices, shipping lanes, defense spending
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack - Brent +15% in 24 hours; current situation is slower-burn but similar magnitude of risk
macro_events.counterargument: Negotiations are ongoing, not collapsed; both sides have incentives to avoid escalation; SPR releases could cap upside

macro_events.title: May CPI Release June 10 - Next Major Catalyst
macro_events.causal_chain: April CPI came in hot at 3.8% YoY with energy +3.8% MoM and shelter +0.6% -> May CPI on June 10 at 8:30 AM ET -> if above 3.5% YoY: cements rate hike narrative, 10Y breaks 4.6%, tech sell-off extends -> if below 3.5%: rate hike odds fall, oversold tech bounces hard, buy-the-dip rotation -> binary event for positioning ahead of June 16-17 FOMC
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic data with global rate market implications
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2022 hot CPI (9.1% YoY) - S&P 500 fell 5.8% in three sessions as rate hike expectations surged
macro_events.counterargument: Base effects from 2025 tariff-driven inflation may cause YoY to optically moderate even if MoM remains elevated
